call_points.text: IGL Spirits targets EBITDA in excess of ₹500 Cr for FY27, with aspirations to become debt-free from FY28
Incremental capex of ₹5-10 Cr expected for FY27, with modular expansion planned as businesses grow
Debt reduction has supported profitable growth, with debt-to-equity ratio improving
JV performance improved with net revenue up 21% QoQ, driven by reduced disadvantage in ethylene oxide pricing
No numeric FY27 revenue or margin guidance was given; management said Chemicals should see improved profitability and top-line growth this year.
About ₹400 crores of FY26 capex went into the Gorakhpur and Kashipur grain distilleries.
A catalyst-change shutdown ran from 17 March to 2 April, cutting production and some sales.
India reached 20% ethanol blending ahead of the original 2030 schedule, driving bio-fuels profit and sales growth.
Performance chemicals value grew 40% and management hopes to more than double that business this year.
The company prepaid about ₹804 crores in Q4FY26, of which ₹467 crores came from the November 2025 equity issue.
FY27 term-loan repayment is about ₹268 crores: ₹168 crores in liquor and ₹100 crores in chemicals.
The war has put oilfield chemicals exports to customers such as New Park largely on hold and raised propylene oxide costs.
Ennature Biopharma's EBITDA improvement may not be significant this financial year as it shifts to value-added customers.
The ₹38.38 crores dividend received from the Clariant JV was adjusted against the investment, not shown as income.
Potable Spirits delivered FY26 revenue of ₹1,331 Cr, up 14.4% YoY, with a 21.4% EBIT margin.
Finance costs declined to ₹26 Cr in Q4FY26 from ₹45 Cr in Q4FY25 on debt reduction.

The CESTAT has already adjudicated in favor of the Company against the order of the Commissioner. Central Excise Duty amounting to Rs.10,39,32,564/- along with applicable interest and penalty. tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: A Show Cause notice was issued by Principal Commissioner alleging incorrect availment of Basic Customs Duty @2.5% instead of 5% during 01.07.2017 to 01.02.2021 on Import of DEA. Upon hearing, the Additional Commissioner had vide Order-in-Original dated 23.03.2024 confirmed an amount of Rs. 33.43 crore as duty paid short along with applicable interest, imposing penalty of Rs. 82 crore and redemption fine of Rs. 191.76 crore under the Customs Act, 1962. Subsequently, the Company filed an appeal before Commissioner (Appeals), Noida, Uttar Pradesh (“Appellate Authority”) against the Impugned Order-in-Original dated 23.03.2024. The Appellate Authority vide its Order-in-Appeal dated 27.02.2026 has partially allowed the Company's appeal and upheld the Impugned Order with respect to demand of Rs. 33.43 crore as duty short paid along with applicable interest and penalty of Rs. 41 crores.The demand for penalty amount of Rs. 41 crore and redemption fine of Rs. 191.76 crore had been set aside. Consequently, there has been a reduction in the substantial amount of total demand against the Company in this matter. Based on the Company’s assessment and advice of the legal counsel, the Company has a strong case on merit and is in process of filing appeal CESTAT, Allahabad against Order-in-Appeal dated 27.02.2026.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Additional Commissioner of Customs, Noida Custom Commissionerate
tax_litigation.status: The Company is in process of filling an appeal against the Order of the Appellate Authority.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Commissioner has filed an appeal challenging the order passed by the Customs, Excise & Service Tax Appellate Tribunal, New Delhi ("CESTAT"), New Delhi, setting aside the Commissioner's earlier order dated 9th May 2019. The Company has not yet received a notice from the Hon'ble High Court of Uttarakhand at Nainital but was informed by its consultant after the matter appeared on the Court's website. The matter pertains to the classification of 'RAB' under the Central Excise Tariff for the financial years 2005 to 2009. The CESTAT has already adjudicated in favor of the Company against the order of the Commissioner. Central Excise Duty amounting to Rs.10,39,32,564/- along with applicable interest and penalty. As the Company has already been awarded a favorable order on this matter by CESTAT, hence the Company, post discussions with the experts, believes that the above demand is not maintainable.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Commissioner of CGST & Central Excise, E-Block, Nehru Colony, Haridwar Road, Dehradun, Uttarakhand (Commissioner).

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company had taken an Insurance Policy covering property damage, machinery breakdown, and consequential business interruption across its plant locations. In 2020, a claim was filed in respect of damaged machinery/equipment at the Kashipur Plant, which was rejected by the Insurance Company despite subsequent representations and submission of requisite documents/information for re-assessment. The claim was repudiated by the Insurance Company on more than one occasion. Based on internal assessment and legal opinion, the Company has initiated steps to challenge the said repudiation before the Hon’ble Delhi High Court for recovery of a claim of Rs. 79.76 Crore (Rupees Seventy-Nine Crore Seventy Six Lakh) towards material damage and loss of profit, along with interest and therefore, had filed an application on 21st May, 2026 for Pre-Institution Mediation and Settlement under the applicable laws.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: The New India Assurance Co. Limited (“Insurance Company”).

Nicotine sales grew two times QoQ driven by customer conversions in Europe and capacity expansion at Kashipur plant

timeline.summary: India Glycols Limited scheduled Q4 & FY26 earnings conference call on May 18, 2026, at 16:00 IST with CEO Rupark Sarswat, CFO Anand Singhal, Head Liquor S.K. Shukla, and Head Legal Ankur Jain.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹2,360.01 Cr, net profit to shareholders ₹86.88 Cr.
India Glycols released its Q4 & FY26 investor presentation showcasing 11.8% growth in net revenue and outlining its demerger restructuring.
India Glycols Limited shared the Q4 & FY26 earnings conference call recording on 18th May 2026 via its website.
On May 21, 2026, India Glycols updated that the NCLT hearing on its demerger scheme was adjourned due to paucity of time.
India Glycols filed an application for pre-institution mediation against New India Assurance to recover a ₹79.76 Cr insurance claim.
India Glycols hosted its Q4 & FY26 earnings conference call detailing segmental performance and debt prepayment.
India Glycols Limited held its Q1FY27 earnings conference call on August 14, 2026, reporting strong revenue and EBITDA growth and announcing NCLT approval for the demerger of its businesses.
